feed.title: The Long View

bullets: Systems thinking in macro means watching feedback loops rather than point estimates — employment data is noisier than headlines suggest, and once internalized, downstream decisions get easier.
Risk management at the central bank level resembles reliability engineering — the framing matters because it tells you which tradeoffs you are making.
The second-order effects of noisy employment data are the part most people miss, especially when teams adopt IEA or IPCC frameworks in their workflows.
Failure modes are harder to spot outside Carbon Trust class tooling — the tradeoffs around risk management crosscut everything else in the conversation.
A practical heuristic for listeners: pick one of the covered ideas and run it for two weeks, with the rest being iteration.
Ignoring feedback loops leads to rebuilding systems from scratch a year later — a pattern observed across multiple teams.
